evidence: Requirement->criterion map built from instruction.md and hireops_rules.md against 2 gate + 40 functional + 5 polish + 5 visual criteria. Mapped and covered: sign-in/workspace (hro_gate_render); shared server-backed create (hro_gate_shared); job fields, places 1-50 integer, HM-only manager (hro_job_open); add candidate bottom of Applied (hro_add_candidate); email validity/case-insensitive dup/other job (hro_add_email_rules); one stage at a time, non-drag (hro_move_one_stage); arrive at bottom (hro_arrive_bottom); manual order shared (hro_reorder); reject reason/rejected-from/Hired refusal/reopen-to-origin/reason cleared/undo restores reason (hro_reject_reason, hro_reject_hired, hro_reopen); Interview places, reorder in full Interview, freed place (hro_interview_full, hro_interview_reorder_free, hro_undo_full); refused put-back with reason and focus (hro_refused_put_back, full-Interview case); role matrix (hro_mgr_late_stages, hro_mgr_early_refused, hro_mgr_other_job, hro_observer_readonly, hro_candidate_no_staff); 401/403/404/409 (hro_anonymous, hro_refusal_status); stale 409 with who (hro_stale_refused); bulk move board order, all-or-none, places for the set (hro_bulk_move, hro_bulk_all_or_none, hro_bulk_places); undo restore/conflict/once/note-not-a-change via B(12) (hro_undo_restores, hro_undo_conflict, hro_undo_once); Activity lines, newest first, job filter, observer read, refusals add nothing (hro_activity, hro_activity_refusals); notes permissions (hro_notes); live board within 15 s (hro_live_board) with open card/note/focus/scroll preserved (hro_pol_live_board); messages exchange live (hro_msg_exchange); blank/Enter/Shift+Enter/line breaks/box empty+focused (hro_msg_compose); failed send kept and explained (hro_pol_failed_send); latest 30, earlier 30 at a time with remaining count, place kept (hro_thread_latest, hro_thread_earlier, hro_pol_earlier_place); draft/focus kept on arrival (hro_pol_live_thread); per-person unread and total, read-at-newest, own messages never unread, send counts as read (hro_unread_counts); scrolled-up notice (hro_unread_scrolled_up); seen incl. observer-never/HM/recruiter (hro_seen); conversation participation (hro_thread_access); drafts per conversation, other view, reload (hro_drafts) and across ended session, re-sign-in, other user on same browser, note drafts (hro_pol_session_resume); candidate list/wording/own conversations (hro_candidate_view), no leaks/404 (hro_candidate_private), account-email link (hro_candidate_linked); seed loaded once, persistence across restart (hro_restart + protocol Z); desktop craft (visual). Bundling of several rules in one criterion was NOT treated as a gap (skill known false positive; workbook internal annotation). UNGRADED asked-for behaviours found (each a gap): (G1) instruction.md:3 'If a move is refused, put the card back where it really is and tell me why; when it is because a colleague moved that card a moment ago, tell me who' and hireops_rules.md:79-80 'The person is told that the card was changed and by whom, and their board shows the card where it really is.' Protocol C (functional/prompt.md:33) only replays the captured request via fetch, so the UI never sees the 409; hro_stale_refused (functional/judge.toml:208) accepts the name 'in the response or on screen'. The on-screen 'tell me who' and the board put-back after a stale refusal are ungraded; hro_refused_put_back covers only the full-Interview refusal. (G2) hireops_rules.md:138 'A message is plain text that is not blank; line breaks are kept.' hro_msg_compose (judge.toml:316-317) grades blank and line breaks but nothing checks that typed markup is shown literally; golden threads.js renders with textContent so the reference would pass such a leg. (G3) hireops_rules.md:84 'A move appears on the mover's board immediately.' No criterion measures that the mover's own successful move shows without waiting for the next live poll; hro_refused_put_back (judge.toml:137) even accepts a UI that refuses before moving, and other move rows have no timing on the mover's own page. (G4) hireops_rules.md:34 'When a save is refused because of the email, say so at that field and keep what was typed.' hro_add_email_rules (judge.toml:47) checks only that 'the typed name stays'; the typed email and source are not checked. Partial/indirect only (Note-level, not counted as gaps): rules:180-181 'signing in does not open one for them' is only indirectly guarded by Lena's starting unread count in hro_unread_counts; instruction.md:7 draft/cursor untouched while scrolled up is graded at the newest message (hro_pol_live_thread) and place-keeping while scrolled up separately (hro_unread_scrolled_up), not jointly. Template runtime policy (PORT honoured, health without DB, Node/Express/SQLite, no shipped DB) is shared runtime/deterministic territory, not judge criteria, per REVIEW_POLICY 'Separate shared runtime policy'; not counted. Static analysis only; no configured judge run exists (raw-evidence-index scope).
counterexample:
A plausible broken app passes every coverage-affected row: (a) its server returns 409 {error:'stale', changed_by:'Mei Lin'} but its board UI on a stale refusal shows only 'Move failed' and leaves the card at the optimistic place until the next poll; hro_stale_refused passes because the name is in the response and the UI path is never exercised (G1). (b) It renders message bodies with innerHTML after replacing newlines with
, so a message 'Offer ' renders as markup/executes; hro_msg_compose still passes (G2). (c) After a successful move it does not re-render and waits for its 10-second poll; every move row still passes because the judge reads the board after the action settles (G3). (d) On a duplicate-email refusal it clears the email and source fields but keeps the name; hro_add_email_rules passes (G4).
suggested_fix: G2: add to hro_msg_compose 'a message containing x is shown with those characters literally'. G4: say 'the typed name and email stay' in hro_add_email_rules. G3: add to hro_move_one_stage (or hro_arrive_bottom) that the mover's page shows the card in its new stage in the first snapshot after the action, before any live-update interval, avoiding sub-second timing. G1: either add a UI-path probe (e.g. in protocol C hold this page's live-update requests with a prescribed page.route/routeWebSocket for that step, have Mei move F, then move F through Rafael's UI and require the person's name on screen and the card shown at its real place) or, if judged infeasible, record an explicit, authorized acceptance that the on-screen 'tell me who' is proxied by the server response. Changing criteria is a new candidate requiring recheck of the other rows.
